extraction_notes.note: Numbered equations (1)-(10) in Section 2 restate later definitions and results (private state, MDI channel, Theorems 2-4, 8, Proposition 2, Eq. (64)); equation (94) restates the relative entropy definition. They get no node.

The proof of Lemma 4 cites Theorem \ref{theo:telecov-weakconv-GE} (Theorem 6) for the 1/K privacy-test bound, which is Theorem 1; since Theorem 6's proof uses Lemma 4 this creates a cycle. The \ref edge is kept and an edge from TP1 to PP20 records the intended dependency.
Labels eq:ds and eq:dl are swapped relative to the depolarizing/dephasing channels they name; edges follow the labels as written.

Protocols (LOCC-assisted key agreement, Devetak-Winter star and chain protocols, breadth-first tree protocol, max-min spanning tree) are described in prose or an enumerate list; extracted as algorithms with unmarked steps.

Proofs of Theorems 5 and 7 and of the MDI-QKD bounds in Appendix F are prose under subsection headings (ended by \qed or the final bound); the proof spans are taken from the first sentence after the heading to the closing formula.
claim or definition: the sentence introduces the cppp capacity and asserts it is at most the LOCC capacity; typed as claim.
Main lower-bound and MDI-QKD capacity results are stated in prose without a theorem environment; typed as claims per the unnamed-prose rule.
Discussion of prior work, figure-only examples and plot descriptions in Appendix H were not extracted beyond the explicit numerical claims and the stated conjecture.

CLM+14.text: Title = {Everything You Always Wanted to Know About {LOCC} (But Were Afraid to Ask)}, Author = {Chitambar, Eric and Leung, Debbie and Man{\v{c}}inska, Laura and Ozols, Maris and Winter, Andreas}, Journal = {Communications in Mathematical Physics}, Year = {2014}, Month = {May}, Note = {arXiv:1210.4583}, Number = {1}, Pages = {303--326}, Volume = {328}, Abstract = {In this paper we study the subset of generalized quantum measurements on finite dimensional systems known as local operations and classical communication (LOCC). While LOCC emerges as the natural class of operations in many important quantum information tasks, its mathematical structure is complex and difficult to characterize. Here we provide a precise description of LOCC and related operational classes in terms of quantum instruments. Our formalism captures both finite round protocols as well as those that utilize an unbounded number of communication rounds. While the set of LOCC is not topologically closed, we show that finite round LOCC constitutes a compact subset of quantum operations. Additionally we show the existence of an open ball around the completely depolarizing map that consists entirely of LOCC implementable maps. Finally, we demonstrate a two-qubit map whose action can be approached arbitrarily close using LOCC, but nevertheless cannot be implemented perfectly.}, Doi = {10.1007/s00220-014-1953-9}, ISSN = {1432-0916}, Owner = {mwilde}, Timestamp = {2016.01.21}, Url = {http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/s00220-

TBR15.text: Title = {Quantum Coding with Finite Resources}, Author = {Marco Tomamichel and Mario Berta and Joseph M. Renes}, Year = {2015}, Month = {April}, Note = {arXiv:1504.04617}, Abstract = {The quantum capacity of a memoryless channel is often used as a single figure of merit to characterize its ability to transmit quantum information coherently. The capacity determines the maximal rate at which we can code reliably over asymptotically many uses of the channel. We argue that this asymptotic treatment is insufficient to the point of being irrelevant in the quantum setting where decoherence severely limits our ability to manipulate large quantum systems in the encoder and decoder. For all practical purposes we should instead focus on the trade-off between three parameters: the rate of the code, the number of coherent uses of the channel, and the fidelity of the transmission. The aim is then to specify the region determined by allowed combinations of these parameters. Towards this goal, we find approximate and exact characterizations of the region of allowed triplets for the qubit dephasing channel and for the erasure channel with classical post-processing assistance. In each case the region is parametrized by a second channel parameter, the quantum channel dispersion. In the process we also develop several general inner (achievable) and outer (converse) bounds on the coding region that are valid for all finite-dimensional quantum channels and can be computed efficiently. Pankowski2010.text: doi = {10.1088/1751-8113/44/3/035301}, url = {https://doi.org/10.1088%2F1751-8113%2F44%2F3%2F035301}, year = 2010, month = {dec}, publisher = {{IOP} Publishing}, volume = {44}, number = {3}, pages = {035301}, author = {{\L}ukasz Pankowski and Micha{\l} Horodecki}, title = {Low-dimensional quite noisy bound entanglement with a cryptographic key}, journal = {Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical}, abstract = {We provide a class of bound entangled states that have a positive distillable secure key rate. The smallest state of this kind is 4⊗4. Our class is a generalization of the class presented in Horodecki et al (2008 IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 54 2621–5). It is much wider, containing, in particular, states from the boundary of PPT entangled states (all of the states in the previous class were of this kind) and also states inside the set of PPT entangled states, even approaching the separable states. This generalization comes at a price: for the wider class, a positive key rate requires, in general, apart from the one-way Devetak–Winter protocol (used in the previous case) also the recurrence preprocessing and thus is effectively a two-way protocol. We also analyze the amount of noise that can be admixtured to the states of our class without losing the key distillability property which may be crucial for experimental realization. The wider class contains key-distillable states with higher entropy (up to 3.524, as opposed to 2.564 for the previous class).} }

nodes.name: Identity operator $\bbm{1}$
nodes.statement: We denote identity operator as $\bbm{1}$.

nodes.name: Systems notation $\vv{A}$, $\vv{B}$, $\vv{C}$, $\vv{K}$
nodes.statement: Let $\vv{A'}\coloneqq \{A_a'\}_{a\in\msc{A}}$, $\vv{A}\coloneqq \{A_a\}_{a\in\msc{A}}$, $\vv{B}=\{B_b\}_{b\in\msc{B}}$, $\vv{C}=\{C_c\}_{c\in\msc{C}}$, $\vv{K}=\{K_i\}_{i=1}^M$, denote sets (compositions) of quantum systems, where $\msc{A},\msc{B},\msc{C}$ are finite sets of symbols such that $|\mc{A}|+|\mc{B}|+|\mc{C}|=M$ for some natural number $M \geq 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Vector notation for the collections of systems held by the parties (senders/receivers $A$, senders $B$, receivers $C$, keys $K$).

nodes.name: Trusted allies $\{\tf{X}_i\}$
Reference systems $\vv{LA}$
nodes.statement: Also, $\vv{LA}$ denotes the set $\{L_aA_a\}_{a\in\msc{A}}$, where $L_a$ is a reference system of $A_a$ and held by $\tf{A}_a$, and same follows for $\vv{RB}$, $\vv{PC}$, and $\vv{SK}$.

nodes.name: Partition notation $:\vv{A}:$
nodes.statement: We use $:\!\vv{A}\!:$ to denote partition with respect to each system in the set $\vv{A}$ as they are held by separate entities, and same follows for $:\!\vv{LA}\!:\!\vv{RB}:$.

nodes.name: GHZ state and EPR (maximally entangled) state
Quantum channel
nodes.statement: A quantum channel $\mc{M}_{B\to C}$ is a completely positive,  trace-preserving map that acts on trace-class operators defined on the Hilbert space $\mc{H}_B$ and uniquely maps them to trace-class operators defined on the Hilbert space $\mc{H}_C$.

nodes.name: Choi state
nodes.statement: For a channel $\mc{M}_{A\to B}$ with $A$ and $B$ as input and output systems, its Choi state $J^\mc{M}_{LB}$ is equal to $\mc{M}(\Phi^+_{LA})$.

nodes.name: Measurement channel (quantum instrument)
LOCC channel
nodes.statement: An LOCC channel $\mc{L}_{\vv{A'}\to \vv{B}}$ can be written as $\sum_{x\in\msc{X}}(\bigotimes_{y\in\msc{Y}}\mc{E}^{y,x}_{A'_y\to B_y})$, where $\vv{A'}=\{A'_{y}\}_y$ and $\vv{B}=\{B_{y}\}_y$ are sets of inputs and outputs, respectively, and $\{\mc{E}^{y,x}\}_{x}$ is a set of completely positive trace non-increasing maps for each $y$ such that $\mc{L}$ is a quantum channel (cf.~\cite{CLM+14}).

nodes.name: Generalized divergence
differentia: it satisfies the following monotonicity (data-processing) inequality for all density operators $\rho$ and $\sigma$ and quantum channels $\mc{N}$

nodes.name: Quantum relative entropy and sandwiched Renyi relative entropy
nodes.statement_short: Quantum relative entropy $D$ and sandwiched R\'enyi relative entropy $\wt{D}_\alpha$ as examples of generalized divergences.
nodes.origin_citation: Umegaki 1962; Muller-Lennert et al. 2013; Wilde, Winter, Yang 2014

nodes.name: Max-relative entropy
$\varepsilon$-hypothesis-testing divergence
Multiplex quantum channel
nodes.statement: Consider multipartite quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ where each pair $A_a', A_a$ is held by a respective party $\tf{A}_a$ and each $B_b,C_c$ are held by parties $\tf{B}_b,\tf{C}_c$, respectively. While $\tf{A}_a$ is both sender and receiver to the channel, $\tf{B}_b$ is only a sender, and $\tf{C}_c$ is only a receiver to the channel. Such a quantum channel is referred to as the multiplex quantum channel. Any two different systems need not be of the same size in general.
differentia: While $\tf{A}_a$ is both sender and receiver to the channel, $\tf{B}_b$ is only a sender, and $\tf{C}_c$ is only a receiver to the channel.
nodes.statement_short: A multipartite channel whose parties are sender-and-receiver ($A$), sender-only ($B$) or receiver-only ($C$).

nodes.name: Conference key state
nodes.statement: A conference key state $\gamma^c_{\vv{K}E}$, with $|K_i|=K$ for all $i\in[M]\coloneqq\{1,…,M\}$, is defined as \begin{align} & \mathcal{D}_{K_1}\otimes\mathcal{D}_{K_2}\otimes\cdots\otimes \mathcal{D}_{K_M}\left(\gamma^c_{\vv{K} E}\right) \coloneqq \nonumber \\ &\qquad \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k\in\msc{K}}\op{k}_{K_1}\otimes \op{k}_{K_2}\otimes\cdots \otimes \op{k}_{K_M}\otimes\sigma_E, \end{align} where $\sigma_E$ is a state of the system $E$, which is accessible to an eavesdropper Eve, $\mathcal{D}(\cdot)=\sum_{k\in\msc{K}}\op{k}(\cdot)\op{k}$ is a projective measurement channel, $\{\ket{k}_{K_i}\}_{k\in\msc{K}}$ forms an orthonormal basis for each $i\in[M]$.
nodes.statement_short: A state whose key systems, after measurement, are perfectly correlated uniform $K$-valued and in product with Eve.
nodes.label: def:key-state

nodes.name: $\varepsilon$-approximate conference key state
Multipartite private state
nodes.statement: A state $\gamma_{\vv{SM}}$, with $|K_i|=K$ for all $i\in[M]$ is called a ($M$-partite) private state if and only if \begin{equation} \gamma_{\vv{SK}}\coloneqq U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}} (\Phi^{\operatorname{GHZ}}_{\vv{K}}\otimes\omega_{\vv{S}}) (U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}})^\dag, \end{equation} where $U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}}\coloneqq \sum_{\vv{k}\in\msc{K}^{\times M}}\op{\vv{k}}_{\vv{K}}\otimes U^{\vv{k}}_{\vv{S}}$ is called a twisting unitary operator for some unitary operator $U^{\vv{k}}_{\vv{S}}$ and $\omega$ is some density operator~\cite{AH09}.
nodes.statement_short: An $M$-partite private state is a twisted GHZ state on key systems tensored with a shield state.
nodes.label: def:multi-priv-state

nodes.name: $\varepsilon$-approximate private state
Form of extensions of private states
assumptions: Any state extension (including purification) $\gamma_{\vv{SK}E}$ of such a private state \eqref{eq:multi-priv-state}

nodes.name: Equivalence of approximate conference key states and approximate private states (AH09 Thm IV.1)
nodes.statement:
It follows from \cite[Theorem~IV.1]{AH09} that 
$F(\gamma^c_{\vv{K} E},\rho_{\vv{K}E})\geq 1-\varepsilon$
implies $F(\gamma_{\vv{SK}},\rho_{\vv{SK}})\geq 1-\varepsilon$, 
and the converse is also true, i.e., $F(\gamma_{\vv{SK}},\rho_{\vv{SK}})\geq 1-\varepsilon$ implies $F(\gamma^c_{\vv{K}E},\rho_{\vv{K}E})\geq 1-\varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Fidelity $\ge 1-\varepsilon$ to a conference key state is equivalent to fidelity $\ge 1-\varepsilon$ to a private state.

nodes.name: $m$-separable pure state
nodes.statement: A pure $n$-partite state that can be written as a tensor product $\ket{\psi_1}\otimes\ket{\psi_2}\otimes...\otimes\ket{\psi_m}$ is called \textit{$m$-separable}.

nodes.name: Fully separable pure state
nodes.statement: If $n=m$, the pure state is said to be fully separable.

nodes.name: Genuinely $n$-partite entangled pure state
nodes.statement: If there is no bipartition with respect to which the pure state is a product state, it is called genuinely $n$-partite entangled.

nodes.name: $m$-separable mixed state
Genuinely multipartite entangled (GME) state
nodes.statement: A  mixed $n$-partite state is considered \textit{genuinely multipartite entangled} (GME) if any decomposition into pure states contains at least one genuinely $n$-partite entangled pure state, i.e. the state is not biseparable.

nodes.name: Free sets FS (fully separable) and BS (biseparable)
nodes.statement: Let a free set $\tf{F}(:\vv{A}:)$ denote the set of all fully separable and biseparable states of system $\vv{A}$ for $\tf{F}=\operatorname{FS}$ and $\tf{F}=\operatorname{BS}$, respectively.

nodes.name: Convexity and LOCC/tensor closure of FS and BS
nodes.statement: Both the sets, $\operatorname{FS}$ and $\operatorname{BS}$, are convex. We note that while $\operatorname{FS}$ is preserved under LOCC operation and tensor product, $\operatorname{BS}$ is preserved under LOCC but not under tensor product, i.e., $\rho^{(x)}_{\vv{A^{(x)}}}\in\operatorname{BS}(:\vv{A^{(x)}}:)$ for $x\in[2]$ but $\rho^{(1)}\otimes\rho^{(2)}$ need not belong to $\operatorname{BS}(:\!\vv{A^{(1)}A^{(2)}}\!:)$.
conclusions: Both the sets, $\operatorname{FS}$ and $\operatorname{BS}$, are convex.
while $\operatorname{FS}$ is preserved under LOCC operation and tensor product, $\operatorname{BS}$ is preserved under LOCC but not under tensor product

nodes.name: Tensor-stable biseparable state
nodes.statement: We refer to biseparable quantum states whose biseparability is preserved under tensor products, i.e. $\rho^{(x)}_{\vv{A^{(x)}}}\in\operatorname{BS}(:\vv{A^{(x)}}:)$ and $\rho^{(1)}\otimes...\otimes\rho^{(n)}\in\operatorname{BS}(:\!\vv{A^{(1)}\ldots A^{(n)}}\!:)$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, as \textit{tensor-stable biseparable} states.
differentia: whose biseparability is preserved under tensor products

nodes.name: Generalized divergence of entanglement / of GME of a state
nodes.statement: The generalized divergence of entanglement $\tf{E}_{\text{E}}$ or genuine mulipartite entanglement (GME) $\tf{E}_\text{GE}$ of an arbitrary state $\rho_{\vv{A}}$ is defined as~\cite{CPV19} \begin{equation} \tf{E}_{r}(:\!\vv{A}\!:)_{\rho}\coloneqq \inf_{\sigma\in\tf{F}(:\!\vv{A}\!:)}\tf{D}(\rho_{\vv{A}}\Vert\sigma_{\vv{A}}), \end{equation} when $\tf{F}=\operatorname{FS}$ or $\tf{F}=\operatorname{BS}$ for $r=\text{E}$ or $r=\text{GE}$, respectively, where $\tf{D}(\rho\Vert\sigma)$ denotes the generalized divergence.
nodes.statement_short: Entanglement (GME) of a state as its generalized-divergence distance to the fully separable (biseparable) set.
nodes.label: def:gen-div-ent

nodes.name: Entangling power of a multiplex channel
nodes.statement: Entangling power of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ with respect to entanglement measure $\tf{E}_{r}$ [Eq. ~\eqref{eq:def-gen-ent}] is defined as the maximum possible gain in the entanglement $\tf{E}_r$ when a quantum state when acted upon by the given channel $\mc{N}$, \begin{align} &\tf{E}_{r}^{p}(\mc{N})\coloneqq\nonumber\\ &\qquad \sup_{\rho}\left[\tf{E}_{r}(:\!\vv{LA}\!:\!\vv{R}\!:\!\vv{PC}\!:)_{\mc{N}(\rho)} -\tf{E}_{r}(:\!\vv{LA'}\!:\!\vv{RB}\!:\!\vv{P}\!:)_{\rho}\right], \end{align} where optimization is over all possible input states $\rho_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Maximal gain of entanglement measure $\tf{E}_r$ achievable by one application of the multiplex channel.

nodes.name: Generalized divergence of entanglement / GME of a multiplex channel
nodes.statement: The generalized divergence of entanglement $\tf{E}_\text{E}(\mc{N})$ or GME $\tf{E}_{\text{GE}}(\mc{N})$ of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ \begin{equation} \tf{E}_{r}(\mc{N})\coloneqq \sup_{\rho\in\operatorname{FS}(:\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:)}\tf{E}_{r}(:\!\vv{LA}\!:\!\vv{R}\!:\!\vv{C}\!:)_{\mc{N}(\rho)}, \end{equation} for $r=\text{E}$ or $r=\text{GE}$, respectively, where $\tf{E}_{r}(:\!\vv{A}\!:)_{\rho}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:def-gen-ent} and GME stands for genuinely multipartite entanglement.
nodes.statement_short: Channel entanglement: supremum over fully separable inputs of the output state's divergence-based entanglement.
nodes.label: def:gen-div-ent-c

nodes.name: Named divergence-based entanglement measures ($r=\text{E}$)
nodes.statement: For $r=\text{E}$, the entanglement measure in \eqref{eq:def-gen-ent} is called $\varepsilon$-hypothesis testing relative entropy of entanglement $E^\varepsilon_{h,\operatorname{E}}$, max-relative entropy of entanglement $E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}$, sandwiched R\`{e}nyi relative entropy of entanglement $\wt{E}_{\alpha, \operatorname{E}}$, or relative entropy of entanglement $E_{\operatorname{E}}$ when the generalized divergence is the $\varepsilon$-hypothesis testing relative entropy, max-relative entropy, sandwiched R\'{enyi} relative entropy, or relative entropy, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Names the entanglement measures obtained from hypothesis-testing, max-, sandwiched R\'enyi and relative entropy.

nodes.name: Named divergence-based GME measures ($r=\text{GE}$)
nodes.statement: For $r=\text{GE}$, the entanglement measure in \eqref{eq:def-gen-ent} is called $\varepsilon$-hypothesis testing relative entropy of GME $E^\varepsilon_{h,\operatorname{GE}}$, max-relative entropy of GME $E_{\max,\operatorname{GE}}$, sandwiched R\`{e}nyi relative entropy of GME $\wt{E}_{\alpha, \operatorname{GE}}$, or relative entropy of GME when the generalized divergence $E_{\operatorname{GE}}$ is the $\varepsilon$-hypothesis testing relative entropy, max-relative entropy, sandwiched R\'{enyi} relative entropy, or relative entropy, respectively. We follow the same procedure for nomenclature of entanglement measures of channels.
nodes.statement_short: Names the GME measures (and channel versions) obtained from the four divergences.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: We note that the sets $\operatorname{FS},\operatorname{BS}$ are convex. Using the data-processed triangle inequality~\cite{CM17} and the argument from the proof of \cite[Proposition~2]{DBW17}, we arrive at the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Data-processed triangle inequality plus the amortization argument of DBW17 Prop. 2.

nodes.name: Amortization collapse for max-relative entropy of entanglement
nodes.statement: The entangling power of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ with respect to the max-relative entropy of entanglement $E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}$ is equal to the max-relative entropy of entanglement of the channel $\mc{N}$, \begin{equation} E_{\max,E}^{p}(\mc{N})=E_{\max,E}(\mc{N}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Entangling power w.r.t. $E_{\max,E}$ equals the channel's max-relative entropy of entanglement.
nodes.label: lem:max-amor

nodes.name: Regularized relative entropy of entanglement of a multiplex channel
nodes.statement_short: Regularized channel divergence of $\mc{N}$ from the set of LOCC channels.

nodes.name: Entangling power bounded by regularized REE
nodes.statement: For finite dimensional Hilbert spaces the entangling power of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ with respect to the relative entropy of entanglement $E_{E}$ is less than or equal to the regularized relative entropy of entanglement of the channel $\mc{N}$, \begin{equation} E_{E}^{p}(\mc{N})\leq E^\infty_{E}(\mc{N}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For finite dimensions the REE entangling power of a multiplex channel is at most its regularized REE.
nodes.label: lem:ree-amor

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Let $\rho_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}}$ be a state and let $\sigma'\in\operatorname{FS}(:\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:\vv{P}:)$. Let $\Lambda_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ an LOCC channel. Then the following inequality holds \begin{multline} E_{E}(:\vv{LA}:\vv{R}:\vv{PC}:)_{\mc{N}(\rho)}\\ \leq D\(\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}(\rho_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}})\Vert \Lambda_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}(\sigma'_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}}) \). \end{multline} Applying the the chain rule from Ref.~\cite{fang2019chain}, we find that \begin{align*} &D\(\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}(\rho_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}})\Vert \Lambda_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}(\sigma'_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}}) \)\\ \leq&D\(\rho_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}}\Vert \sigma'_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}} \)\\ & +D^{\infty}\(\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}\Vert \Lambda_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}\). \end{align*} Since the above holds for arbitrary fully separable states $\sigma'_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}}$ and arbitrary LOCC channels $\Lambda_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$, we arrive at \begin{multline} E_{E}(:\vv{LA}:\vv{R}:\vv{PC}:)_{\mc{N}(\rho)}\\ \leq E_{E}(:\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:\vv{P}:)_{\rho}+ E^\infty_{E}(\mc{N}), \end{multline} finishing the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Bound REE by divergence to an LOCC-processed separable state, then apply the chain rule of Fang et al.

nodes.name: Fix input, separable state and LOCC channel
nodes.statement: Let $\rho_{\vv{LA'}\vv{RB}\vv{P}}$ be a state and let $\sigma'\in\operatorname{FS}(:\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:\vv{P}:)$. Let $\Lambda_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ an LOCC channel.
nodes.statement_short: Fix an input state, a fully separable state and an LOCC channel.

nodes.name: REE bounded by divergence to LOCC image
nodes.statement_short: Bound the output REE by divergence to the LOCC image of a separable state.

nodes.name: Chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Apply the chain rule of Fang et al.

nodes.name: Optimize
nodes.statement_short: Optimize over separable states and LOCC channels.

nodes.name: Optimization over pure input states suffices
nodes.statement: It suffices to optimize $E^\varepsilon_{h,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N})$, $E^\varepsilon_{h,\operatorname{GE}}(\mc{N})$, $E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N})$, $E_{E,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N})$ and $E_{\max,\operatorname{GE}}(\mc{N})$ of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}$ over all pure input states, i.e., $\rho\in\operatorname{FS}(:\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:)$ is a pure state in \eqref{eq:def-gen-ent-c} for $E^\varepsilon_{h,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N}),E^\varepsilon_{h,\operatorname{GE}}(\mc{N}), E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N}), E_{E,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N}), E_{\max,\operatorname{GE}}(\mc{N})$. This reduction follows from the quasi-convexity of the max-relative entropy~\cite{D09} and $\varepsilon$-hypothesis testing relative entropy~\cite{TT13}, as well as the convexity of the relative entropy of entanglement~\cite{VP98}. Namely, the maximum of a (quasi)-convex function over a convex set will be attained on a boundary point. The boundary points of the set of fully separable density matrices are given by the fully separable pure states.
nodes.statement_short: Channel entanglement measures can be optimized over pure fully separable inputs by (quasi-)convexity.

nodes.name: $\gamma$-privacy test
nodes.statement:
A $\gamma$-privacy test corresponding to $\gamma_{\vv{SK}}$ is defined as the dichotomic measurement~\cite{WTB16}
$\{\Pi^{\gamma}_{\vv{SK}},\bbm{1}-\Pi^{\gamma}_{\vv{SK}}\}$, where $\Pi^{\gamma}_{\vv{SK}}\coloneqq U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}} (\Phi_{\vv{K}}\otimes\bbm{1}_{\vv{S}}) (U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}})^\dag$.

nodes.name: Approximate private states pass the privacy test
nodes.statement: If a state $\rho_{\vv{SK}}$ is $\varepsilon$-approximate to $\gamma_{\vv{SK}}$, i.e., $F(\rho_{\vv{SK}},\gamma_{\vv{SK}})\geq 1-\varepsilon$ then $\rho_{\vv{KS}}$ passes $\gamma$-privacy test with success probability $ 1-\varepsilon$, i.e., \begin{equation} \operatorname{Tr}[\Pi^{\gamma}_{\vv{SK}}\rho_{\vv{SK}}] \geq 1-\varepsilon. \end{equation}
nodes.label: thm:priv-test

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: \begin{align} & \operatorname{Tr}[\Pi^{\gamma}_{\vv{SK}}\rho_{\vv{SK}}]\nonumber \\ & \quad = \bra{\Phi^{\operatorname{GHZ}}}_{\vv{K}}\operatorname{Tr}_{\vv{S}}[(U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}})^\dag \rho_{\vv{SK}}U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}}]\ket{\Phi^{\operatorname{GHZ}}}_{\vv{K}}\\ &\quad = F\(\Phi^{\operatorname{GHZ}}_{\vv{K}},\operatorname{Tr}_{\vv{S}}[(U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}})^\dag \rho_{\vv{SK}}U^{\text{tw}}_{K_1\ldots K_MS_1\ldots S_M}]\)\\ &\quad \geq F\(\Phi^{\operatorname{GHZ}}_{\vv{K}}\otimes\omega_{\vv{S}},(U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}})^\dag \rho_{\vv{SK}}U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}}\)\\ &\quad = F\(U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}} \Phi^{\operatorname{GHZ}}_{\vv{K}}\otimes\omega_{\vv{S}}(U^{\text{tw}}_{\vv{SK}})^\dag, \rho_{\vv{SK}}\)\\ & \quad =F(\gamma_{\vv{SK}},\rho_{\vv{SK}})\geq 1-\varepsilon . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the test probability as a fidelity and use monotonicity of fidelity under partial trace.

nodes.name: Biseparable states fail every privacy test (private states are GME)
nodes.statement: A biseparable state $\sigma_{\vv{SK}}\in\operatorname{BS}(:\!\vv{SK}\!:)$ can never pass any $\gamma$-privacy test with probability greater $1/K$, i.e., \begin{align} \operatorname{Tr}[\Pi^{\gamma}_{\vv{SK}}\sigma_{\vv{SK}}]\leq \frac{1}{K}. \end{align}
conclusions: can never pass any $\gamma$-privacy test with probability greater $1/K$
nodes.statement_short: Any biseparable state passes a $\gamma$-privacy test with probability at most $1/K$; hence private states are GME.
nodes.label: thm:priv-gme

nodes.name: Eve holds the channel environment and the classical communication
nodes.statement: Environment part $E$ of an isometric extension $U^\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}E}$ of the channel $\mc{N}$ is accessible to Eve along with all classical information communicated among $\tf{X}_i$ while performing LOCC.

nodes.name: Local systems of trusted parties are secure from Eve
nodes.statement: All other quantum systems that are locally available to $\tf{X}_i$ are said to be secure from Eve, i.e., even if local operations during LOCC are noisy, purifying quantum systems are still within labs of trusted allies, which are off-limits for Eve.

nodes.name: LOCC-assisted secret key agreement protocol over a multiplex channel
nodes.statement: In the first round, all $\tf{X}_i$ perform LOCC $\mc{L}^1$ to generate a state $\rho_1\in\operatorname{FS}(:\!\vv{L^{(1)}A^{(1)'}}:\!\vv{R^{(1)}B^{(1)}}\!:\!\vv{P^{(1)}})$. All $\tf{A}_a$ and $\tf{B}_b$ input respective systems to multiplex channel $\mc{N}^1_{\vv{A^{(1)'}}\vv{B^{(1)}}\to \vv{C}^{(1)}}$, and let $\tau_1\coloneqq \mc{N}^1(\rho)$ be the output state after the first use $\mc{N}^{1}$ of multiplex channel. In the second round, an LOCC $\mc{L}^{2}$ is performed on $\tau_1$ and then second use $\mc{N}^{2}$ of multiplex channel is employed on $\rho_2\coloneqq \mc{L}^{2}(\tau_1)$. In the third round, an LOCC $\mc{L}^{3}$ is performed on $\tau_2\coloneqq \mc{N}^2(\rho_2)$ and then the third use $\mc{N}^{3}$ of multiplex channel is employed on $\rho_3\coloneqq \mc{L}^{3}(\tau_2)$. Successively, we continue this procedure for $n$ rounds, where an $\mc{L}$ acts on the output state of previous round, after which multiplex channel is performed on the resultant state. Finally, after $n^{\text{th}}$ round, an LOCC $\mc{L}^{n+1}$ is performed as a decoding channel, which generates the final state $\omega_{\vv{SK}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Interleave $n$ uses of the multiplex channel with LOCC rounds, then apply a final LOCC decoder to obtain $\omega_{\vv{SK}}$.

nodes.name: Initial LOCC
nodes.statement: In the first round, all $\tf{X}_i$ perform LOCC $\mc{L}^1$ to generate a state $\rho_1\in\operatorname{FS}(:\!\vv{L^{(1)}A^{(1)'}}:\!\vv{R^{(1)}B^{(1)}}\!:\!\vv{P^{(1)}})$.
nodes.statement_short: Generate a fully separable state by LOCC $\mc{L}^1$.

nodes.name: First channel use
nodes.statement: All $\tf{A}_a$ and $\tf{B}_b$ input respective systems to multiplex channel $\mc{N}^1_{\vv{A^{(1)'}}\vv{B^{(1)}}\to \vv{C}^{(1)}}$, and let $\tau_1\coloneqq \mc{N}^1(\rho)$ be the output state after the first use $\mc{N}^{1}$ of multiplex channel.
nodes.statement_short: Feed the inputs into the first channel use.

nodes.name: Second round
nodes.statement: In the second round, an LOCC $\mc{L}^{2}$ is performed on $\tau_1$ and then second use $\mc{N}^{2}$ of multiplex channel is employed on $\rho_2\coloneqq \mc{L}^{2}(\tau_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: LOCC then second channel use.

nodes.name: Third round
nodes.statement: In the third round, an LOCC $\mc{L}^{3}$ is performed on $\tau_2\coloneqq \mc{N}^2(\rho_2)$ and then the third use $\mc{N}^{3}$ of multiplex channel is employed on $\rho_3\coloneqq \mc{L}^{3}(\tau_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: LOCC then third channel use.

nodes.name: Repeat for $n$ rounds
nodes.statement: Successively, we continue this procedure for $n$ rounds, where an $\mc{L}$ acts on the output state of previous round, after which multiplex channel is performed on the resultant state.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate LOCC and channel use for $n$ rounds.

nodes.name: Decoding LOCC
nodes.statement: Finally, after $n^{\text{th}}$ round, an LOCC $\mc{L}^{n+1}$ is performed as a decoding channel, which generates the final state $\omega_{\vv{SK}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Final LOCC decoder outputs $\omega_{\vv{SK}}$.

nodes.name: LOCC-assisted protocols can be purified
nodes.statement: It can be concluded from the equivalence between private states, and CK states that any protocol of the above form can be purified, i.e., by considering isometric extensions of all channels (LOCC and $\mc{N}$) (the proof arguments are the same as for the purified protocol for LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement~\cite{DBW17}).
conclusions: any protocol of the above form can be purified

nodes.name: $(n,K,\varepsilon)$ LOCC-assisted secret key agreement protocol
nodes.statement: At the end of the purified protocol, Eve posses all the environment systems $E^n$ from isometric extension $U^\mc{N}$ of each use of multiplex channel $\mc{N}$ along with coherent copies $Y^{n+1}$ of the classical data exchanged among trusted parties $\tf{X}_i$ during performances of $n+1$ LOCC channels. Whereas, each trusted party $\tf{X}_i$ posses the key system $K_i$ and the shield system $S_i$, which consists of all local reference systems, after the action of decoder. The state at the end of the protocol is a pure state $\omega_{\vv{SK}Y^{n+1}E^n}$ with $F(\gamma_{\vv{SK}},\omega_{\vv{SK}})\geq 1-\varepsilon$. Such a protocol is called an $(n,K,\varepsilon)$ LOCC-assisted secret key agreement protocol.
nodes.statement_short: A purified protocol whose final state on keys and shields has fidelity at least $1-\varepsilon$ with a private state of $\log_2K$ bits.

nodes.name: Rate of a protocol
Achievable rate
nodes.statement: A rate $P$ is achievable if for $\varepsilon\in(0,1),\delta>0$, and sufficiently large $n$, there exists an $(n,2^{n(P-\delta)},\varepsilon)$ LOCC-assisted secret key agreement protocol.

nodes.name: LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity
nodes.statement: The LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity $\hat{P}_{\operatorname{LOCC}}(\mc{N})$ of a multiplex quantum channel $\mc{N}$ is defined as the supremum of all achievable rates.

nodes.name: Strong converse rate
nodes.statement: A rate $P$ is called a strong converse rate for LOCC-assisted secret key agreement if for all $\varepsilon\in[0,1), \delta>0$, and sufficiently large $n$, there does not exist an $(n, 2^{n(P+\delta)},\varepsilon)$ LOCC-assisted secret key agreement protocol.

nodes.name: Strong converse LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity
nodes.statement: The strong converse LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity $\widetilde{P}_{\operatorname{LOCC}}(\mc{N})$ is defined as the infimum of all strong converse rates.

nodes.name: cppp-assisted secret key agreement
nodes.statement: We can also consider the whole development discussed above for conference key agreement assisted only with classical preprocessing and postprocessing (cppp) communication, i.e., all parties are allowed only two LOCC channels, one for encoding and the other for decoding.

nodes.name: $(n,K,\varepsilon)$ cppp-assisted protocol
nodes.statement: A $(n,K,\varepsilon)$ cppp-assisted secret key agreement protocol over $\mc{N}$ is same as a $(1,K,\varepsilon)$ LOCC-assisted secret key agreement protocol over channel $\mc{N}^{\otimes n}$, and for $n=1$ both protocol are the same.

nodes.name: cppp capacity is at most LOCC capacity
Maximal $n$-use cppp rate $\hat{P}^{\mc{N}}_{\textnormal{cppp}}(n,\varepsilon)$
nodes.statement:
Let $
\hat{P}^{\mc{N}}_{\textnormal{cppp}}(n,\varepsilon)$ be the maximum rate such that $(n,2^{nP},\varepsilon)$ cppp-assisted secret key agreement is achievable for any given $\mc{N}$.

nodes.name: Key rate dominates GHZ distillation rate
nodes.statement: It should be noted that the maximum rate at which secret key can be distilled using LOCC- or cppp-assisted protocol over a multiplex channel $\mc{N}$ is never less than the maximum rate at which GHZ state can be distilled using LOCC- or cppp-assisted protocol over given channel $\mc{N}$, respectively. This statement holds because GHZ state is a special private state from which secret bits are readily accessible to trusted allies.

nodes.name: Constrained protocols and capacities
nodes.statement: Different physical constraints can be invoked in communication protocols to define constrained protocols and associated capacities. For instance, we can invoke energy constraints on input states and detectors to get energy-constrained protocols and respective capacities (cf.~\cite{GES16,WQ18}).

nodes.name: One-shot cppp converse bound via hypothesis-testing GME
nodes.statement: For any fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the achievable region of cppp-assisted secret key agreement over a single use of multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ satisfies \begin{equation} \hat{P}_{\textnormal{cppp}}^{\mc{N}}(1,\varepsilon)\leq E^\varepsilon_{h,\operatorname{GE}}(\mc{N}), \end{equation} where \begin{equation} E^{\varepsilon}_{h,\operatorname{GE}}(\mc{N}) \coloneqq \sup_{\psi\in\operatorname{FS}(:\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:)}\inf_{\sigma\in\operatorname{BS}(:\vv{LA}:\vv{R}:\vv{C}:)} D^\varepsilon_h(\mc{N}(\psi)\Vert\sigma) \end{equation} is the $\varepsilon$-hypothesis testing relative entropy of genuine entanglement of the multiplex channel $\mc{N}$. It suffices to optimize over pure input states $\psi\in\operatorname{FS}(:\!\vv{LA'}\!:\!\vv{RB}\!:)$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Privacy from a single-use of a multiplex channel
assumptions: cppp-assisted secret key agreement over a single use of multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$
conclusions: It suffices to optimize over pure input states $\psi\in\operatorname{FS}(:\!\vv{LA'}\!:\!\vv{RB}\!:)$.
nodes.statement_short: One-shot cppp-assisted key rate is at most the channel's $\varepsilon$-hypothesis-testing relative entropy of GME.
nodes.label: thm:one-shot-cppp

nodes.name: Weak converse on cppp-assisted capacity
nodes.statement: A weak converse bound on the cppp-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}$ is given by \begin{align} \hat{P}_{\textnormal{cppp}}(\mc{N})& = \inf_{\varepsilon\in (0,1)}\liminf_{n\to\infty}\hat{P}^{\mc{N}}_{\textnormal{cppp}}(n,\varepsilon)\\ &\leq E^{\infty}_{\operatorname{GE}}(\mc{N}). \end{align}
nodes.section: 5.1 Privacy from a single-use of a multiplex channel
nodes.statement_short: The cppp-assisted capacity is bounded by the regularized relative entropy of GME of the channel.

nodes.name: Zero cppp capacity for tensor-stable biseparable outputs
nodes.statement: Consider a class of multiplex channels $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ such that for all pure input states $\psi\in\operatorname{FS}(\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:\vv{P})$, the output states $\mc{N}(\psi)$ are tensor-stable biseparable states with respect to the partition $\vv{LA}:\vv{RB}:\vv{PC}$. The cppp-assisted secret-key-agreement capacities for such class of multiplex channels are zero.
nodes.section: 5.1 Privacy from a single-use of a multiplex channel
assumptions: for all pure input states $\psi\in\operatorname{FS}(\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:\vv{P})$, the output states $\mc{N}(\psi)$ are tensor-stable biseparable states with respect to the partition $\vv{LA}:\vv{RB}:\vv{PC}$
conclusions: The cppp-assisted secret-key-agreement capacities for such class of multiplex channels are zero.

nodes.name: Strong converse bound via max-relative entropy of entanglement
nodes.statement: For a fixed $n,\ K\in\mathbb{N},\ \varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the following bound holds for an $(n,K,\varepsilon)$ protocol for LOCC-assisted secret key agreement over a multiplex $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$: \begin{equation} \frac{1}{n}\log_2K\leq E_{\max,E}(\mc{N})+ \frac{1}{n}\log_2\left(\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon}\right), \end{equation} where the max-relative entropy of entanglement $E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N})$ of the multiplex channel $\mc{N}$ is \begin{equation*} E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N}) \coloneqq \sup_{\psi\in\operatorname{FS}(:\vv{LA'}:\vv{RB}:)}\inf_{\sigma\in\operatorname{FS}(:\vv{LA}:\vv{R}:\vv{C}:)} D_{\max}(\mc{N}(\psi)\Vert\sigma) \end{equation*} and it suffices to optimize over pure states $\psi$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Strong converse bounds on LOCC-assisted private capacity of multiplex channel
assumptions: an $(n,K,\varepsilon)$ protocol for LOCC-assisted secret key agreement over a multiplex $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$
nodes.statement_short: Rate of any $(n,K,\varepsilon)$ LOCC-assisted protocol is at most $E_{\max,E}(\mc{N})$ plus a $\frac1n\log\frac1{1-\varepsilon}$ term.
nodes.label: thm:emax-key-converse

nodes.name: Exponential decay of fidelity above $E_{\max,E}$
nodes.statement: The bound in \eqref{eq:emax-key-converse} can also be rewritten as \begin{equation} 1-\varepsilon \leq 2^{-n (P-E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N}))}, \end{equation} where we have $P=\frac{1}{n}\log_2 K$. Thus, if the secret-key-agreement rate $P$ is strictly greater than the max-relative entropy of entanglement $E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N})$ of the (multiplex) channel $\mc{N}$, then the fidelity of the distillation $(1-\varepsilon)$ decays exponentially fast to zero in the number of channel uses.
nodes.section: 5.2 Strong converse bounds on LOCC-assisted private capacity of multiplex channel
nodes.statement_short: Rewriting Theorem 3: fidelity decays exponentially when the rate exceeds $E_{\max,E}(\mc{N})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3 (from Remark 4)
nodes.statement: An immediate corollary of the above remark is the following strong converse statement.
nodes.section: 5.2 Strong converse bounds on LOCC-assisted private capacity of multiplex channel
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the exponential fidelity decay in Remark 4.

nodes.name: Strong converse capacity bounded by $E_{\max,E}$
nodes.statement: The strong converse LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}$ is bounded from above by its max-relative entropy of entanglement: \begin{equation} \wt{P}_{\operatorname{LOCC}}(\mc{N})\leq E_{\max,E}(\mc{N}). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.2 Strong converse bounds on LOCC-assisted private capacity of multiplex channel

nodes.name: Strong converse bound via regularized relative entropy of entanglement
nodes.statement: For finite Hilbert space dimensions the asymptotic LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ is bounded by its regularized relative entropy of entanglement: \begin{equation} \widetilde{\mc{P}}_{\operatorname{LOCC}}(\mc{N})\leq E_{E}^\infty(\mc{N}). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.2 Strong converse bounds on LOCC-assisted private capacity of multiplex channel
nodes.statement_short: For finite dimensions the strong converse LOCC-assisted capacity is at most the regularized REE of the channel.
nodes.label: thm:ree-key-converse

nodes.name: Teleportation-simulable multiplex channel
nodes.statement: A multipartite quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ is teleportation-simulable with associated resource state $\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}$, where $R_b\simeq B_b$ for all $b\in\msc{B}$ and $L_a\simeq A'_a$ for all $a\in\msc{A}$, if for all input states $\rho_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}}$ the following identity holds \begin{equation} \mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}(\rho_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}})=\mc{T}_{\vv{A'LA}\vv{BR}\vv{C}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}(\rho_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}}\otimes\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}) \end{equation} for some LOCC channel $\mc{T}$ with input partition $:\vv{A'LA}:\vv{BR}:\vv{C}:$ and output partition $:\vv{A}:\vv{C}:$.
nodes.statement_short: A channel equal to an LOCC acting on the input and a fixed resource state.

nodes.name: Covariant multiplex channel
nodes.statement_short: Input unitaries from group representations can be pushed through the channel as output unitaries.

nodes.name: Tele-covariant channel
nodes.statement: A quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ is called tele-covariant if it is covariant with respect to groups $\{\msc{G}_a\}_{a\in\msc{A}}$ and $\{\msc{G}_b\}_{b\in\msc{B}}$ that have representations as unitary one-designs, i.e., for all $a\in\msc{A}$ and $b\in\msc{B}$ as well as states $\rho_{A'_a}$ and $\rho_{B_b}$, it holds $\frac{1}{G_a}\sum_{g_a\in\msc{G}_a}\mathcal{U}_{A'_a}^{g_a}(\rho_{A'_a})=\bbm{1}/|A_a|$ and $\frac{1}{G_b}\sum_{g_b\in\msc{G}_b}\mathcal{U}_{B_b}^{g_b}(\rho_{B_b})=\bbm{1}/|B_b|$, respectively.
differentia: groups $\{\msc{G}_a\}_{a\in\msc{A}}$ and $\{\msc{G}_b\}_{b\in\msc{B}}$ that have representations as unitary one-designs
nodes.label: def:tele-cov

nodes.name: Composition and tensor products preserve tele-covariance
nodes.statement: Tele-covariance of a channel is with respect to the groups and their unitary representations on the input and output Hilbert spaces of the channel. If associated unitary representations for the tele-covariant channels $\mc{N}^1$ and $\mc{N}^2$ are respectively same on the output Hilbert spaces of $\mc{N}^1$ that are also the input Hilbert spaces for $\mc{N}^2$, then the composition channel $\mc{N}=\mc{N}^2\circ\mc{N}^1$ is also tele-covariant. A quantum channel obtained by the tensor-product (super-operation ``~$\otimes$", which physically means parallel uses) of tele-covariant channels is also a tele-covariant channel.
nodes.label: rem:comp

nodes.name: Tele-covariant channels are teleportation-simulable via their Choi state
nodes.statement: If a multipartite channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ is tele-covariant, then it is teleportation-simulable with resource state~\eqref{eq:tele-sim} as its Choi state, i.e., $\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}=\mc{N}(\Phi^+_{\vv{L}\vv{R}|\vv{A'}\vv{B}})$.
conclusions: it is teleportation-simulable with resource state~\eqref{eq:tele-sim} as its Choi state
nodes.label: thm:bicov

nodes.name: Capacity bound for teleportation-simulable channels via regularized REE of GME
nodes.statement: The LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity of a multiplex quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ which is teleportation-simulable with resource state $\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}$ is upper bounded as \begin{equation} \hat{P}_{\operatorname{LOCC}}(\mc{N})\leq E^{\infty}_{GE}(:\vv{LA}:\vv{R}:\vv{C}:)_{\theta}, \end{equation} where $E^\infty(:\vv{A}:)_{\rho}$ is the regularized relative entropy of entanglement of state $\rho_{\vv{A}}$.
assumptions: a multiplex quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ which is teleportation-simulable with resource state $\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}$
nodes.label: theo:telecov-weakconv-GE

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4
nodes.statement: Using the above theorem, we immediately get the following corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Theorem 6 since the regularized GME of a tensor-stable biseparable state vanishes.

nodes.name: Zero capacity for channels simulable with tensor-stable biseparable resources
nodes.statement: For a multiplex quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$, which is teleportation-simulable with a tensor-stable biseparable resource state it holds $\hat{P}_{\operatorname{LOCC}}(\mc{N})=0$.
assumptions: a multiplex quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$, which is teleportation-simulable with a tensor-stable biseparable resource state

nodes.name: Sandwiched Renyi bound for teleportation-simulable channels
nodes.statement: For a fixed $n,\ K\in\mathbb{N},\ \varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the following bound holds for an $(n,M,\varepsilon)$ protocol for LOCC-assisted secret key agreement over a multiplex teleportation-simulable quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ with associated resource state $\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}$, $\forall \alpha>1$, \begin{equation} \frac{1}{n} \log_2 K \leq \widetilde{E}_{\alpha,E} (:\vv{LA}:\vv{R}:\vv{C}:)_{\theta} +\frac{\alpha}{n(\alpha-1)}\log_2 \!\( \frac{1}{1-\varepsilon}\). \end{equation}
assumptions: a multiplex teleportation-simulable quantum channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ with associated resource state $\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}$
nodes.statement_short: Key rate over a teleportation-simulable channel is bounded by the sandwiched R\'enyi REE of the resource state plus a vanishing term.
nodes.label: theo:E-alpha_bound

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5
nodes.statement: Setting $\alpha=1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ and letting $n\to\infty$, we obtain
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\alpha=1+1/\sqrt{n}$ in Theorem 7 and let $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Capacity of teleportation-simulable channels bounded by REE of resource state
nodes.statement: The LOCC-assisted secret-key-agreement capacity of a multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ which is teleportation-simulable with resource state $\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}$ is upper bounded as \begin{equation} \hat{P}_{\operatorname{LOCC}}(\mc{N})\leq E_E(:\vv{LA}:\vv{R}:\vv{C}:)_{\theta}, \end{equation} where $E(:\vv{A}:)_{\rho}$ is the relative entropy of entanglement of state $\rho_{\vv{A}}$; this bound is also a strong converse bound.
assumptions: a multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ which is teleportation-simulable with resource state $\theta_{\vv{LA}\vv{R}\vv{C}}$
conclusions: this bound is also a strong converse bound
nodes.label: thm:tele

nodes.name: MDI-QKD multiplex channel $\mc{N}^{\text{MDI}}$
nodes.statement:
A way to incorporate such protocols in our scenario is to identify Alice and Bob as two trusted parties and include the measurement performed by the relay, as well as channels ${\mc N}^{1,2}$, into a bipartite quantum-classical (qc) channel 
\begin{equation} \mc{N}^{\text{MDI}}_{A'B'\to Z_AZ_B}\coloneqq\mc{B}_{X\to Z_AZ_B}\circ\mc{M}_{AB\to X}\circ{\mc N}^1_{A'\to A}\otimes{\mc N}^2_{B'\to B},
\end{equation}
where $\mc{M}_{AB\to x}$ is the quantum instrument (channel) performing a POVM $\{\Lambda^x\}_x$ and writing the output $x$ into a classical register $X$ and $\mc{B}_{X\to Z_AZ_B}$ a classical broadcast channel sending input $x$ to $Z_A$ and $Z_B$. Registers $Z_A$ and $Z_B$ are received by Alice and Bob respectively.
nodes.statement_short: MDI-QKD as a bipartite quantum-classical channel: two links, a relay measurement, and a classical broadcast.

nodes.name: Bounds for MDI-QKD from the general converse theorems
nodes.statement: Application of Theorem \ref{thm:emax-key-converse} for arbitrary systems and Theorem \ref{thm:ree-key-converse} for finite-dimensional systems (as well as the results of Ref.~\cite{DBW17,BDW18,D18thesis}), then provides bounds on the achievable key rate in terms of $E_{\max,\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N}^{\text{MDI}}_{A'B'\to Z_AZ_B})$ and $E^\infty_{\operatorname{E}}(\mc{N}^{\text{MDI}}_{A'B'\to Z_AZ_B})$, respectively, which can be seen as measures of the entangling capabilities of the the measurement $\{\Lambda^x\}_x$. The multiplex quantum channel $\mc{N}^{\text{MDI}}_{A'B'\to Z_AZ_B}$ is tele-covariant if $\mc{N}_{1,2}$ as well as $\mc{M}$ are tele-covariant and the bound reduces to the relative entropy of entanglement of the Choi state of $\mc{N}^{\text{MDI}}_{A'B'\to Z_AZ_B}$.

nodes.name: MDI conference key agreement as a multiplex channel
nodes.statement: We assume a setup of MDI conference agreement, where a number of trusted parties $\tf{A}_i$, for $i\in[n]$,  locally prepare a states which they send to a central relay via channels ${\mc N}^1_{A'_1\to A_1},...,{\mc N}^n_{A'_n\to A_n}$. At the relay a joint measurement is performed on $A_1A_2...A_n$, the result of which is broadcasted back to the trusted parties. It is straightforward to generalize ~\eqref{eq:MDIchannel} to the multipartite case and apply Theorems \ref{thm:emax-key-converse} and \ref{thm:ree-key-converse} (or Theorem \ref{thm:tele} for tele-covariant channels)  to obtain bounds on the conference key rates.

nodes.name: Repeater channel (no error correction)
Repeater channel with one-way error correction
Repeater chain channel
nodes.statement: By recursively combining the bipartite channels ${\mc N}^{\text{repeater}}$, it is possible to derive a bipartite channel ${\mc N}^{\text{repeater chain}}$ between Alice and Bob that includes a repeater chain with an arbitrary amount of repeater stations.

nodes.name: Upper bounds for key repeaters
nodes.statement: Using the results of Refs.~\cite{DBW17,BDW18,D18thesis}, or Theorem \ref{thm:ree-key-converse}, we can obtain upper bounds for key repeater protocols that only involve one-way classical communication from Charlie to Alice and Bob, as have been considered in Refs.~\cite{bauml2015limitations,christandl2017private}. The bounds are given by $\min\{ E_{\max,E}(\mc{N}^{\text{repeater (chain)}}),E^{\infty}_{E}(\mc{N}^{\text{repeater (chain)}}\}$. By Remark~\ref{rem:comp}, if $\mc{N}_{1,2}$ as well as $\mc{M}$ are tele-covariant, so will be $\mc{N}^{\text{repeater (chain)}}$. Hence, by Theorem \ref{thm:tele}, the bound reduces to the relative entropy of entanglement of the Choi state of $\mc{N}^{\text{repeater (chain)}}$. Note that, whereas the bounds in Refs.~\cite{bauml2015limitations,christandl2017private} only depend on the initial states shared by Alice and Charlie as well as  Bob and Charlie, the formulation in terms of a bipartite channel can provide bounds that also depend on the measurement performed by Charlie, as well as operations performed during error correction. The new bounds take into account imperfect measurements and error correction, which provide an additional limitation on the obtainable rate in practical implementations. Our bounds can at least shown to be comparable with the results of Refs.~\cite{bauml2015limitations,christandl2017private} under certain situations of practical interest. For an example, our bound is certainly better when ${\mc N}_1^{A\to C_A}$ and ${\mc N}_2^{B\to C_B}$ are identity channels, allowing Alice and Charlie as well as  Bob and Charlie to share maximally entangled states, whereas Charlie's measurement is noisy.
nodes.statement_short: Repeater key rates are bounded by min of $E_{\max,E}$ and $E^\infty_E$ of the repeater channel; REE of its Choi state when tele-covariant.

nodes.name: Pure-loss bosonic channel noise model
nodes.statement: We assume a noise model for the transmission of a photon through the optical fiber to be a pure-loss bosonic channel with transmissivity $\eta$.

nodes.name: Pure-loss channel on dual-rail qubits acts as an erasure channel
nodes.statement: The action of this pure-loss channel on qubit encoded with our dual-rail scheme is identical to an erasure channel~\cite{GBP97} $\mathcal{E}$ with erasure parameter $1-\eta$ and erasure state $\ket{e}$, where $\ket{e}$ is the vacuum state, i.e., zero photon in both modes.
conclusions: identical to an erasure channel~\cite{GBP97} $\mathcal{E}$ with erasure parameter $1-\eta$ and erasure state $\ket{e}$
nodes.origin_citation: Grassl, Beth, Pellizzari 1997; Das et al. 2018 (DKD18)

nodes.name: Erasure channel is tele-covariant
nodes.statement: We note that an erasure channel is tele-covariant.

nodes.name: Relay Bell measurement succeeds with probability $q$
nodes.statement: We make a simplistic noise model assumption on the measurement channel $\mathcal{M}_{\vv{C_i}\to X}$ by Charlie: it can perform perfect qubit Bell-measurement for bipartite MDI-QKD, respectively, with probability $q$. Whereas with probability $1-q$ for the failed measurement, we assume the relay station signals $\op{\perp}_{X}$ to the users.

nodes.name: Noiseless classical communication
nodes.statement: In addition, we can safely assume classical communication $X\to \vv{Z}$ among all parties to be clean (noiseless) as they do not require any quantum resource.

nodes.name: Perfect local error correction
nodes.statement: Finally, for simplicity, we assume error-correcting local operations for all parties can be made perfectly.

nodes.name: Derivation of the REE of the erasure MDI-QKD Choi state
nodes.statement_short: Compute the Choi state of the erasure-link MDI channel with a probabilistic Bell measurement; its REE is $q\eta_1\eta_2$.

nodes.name: Reduce to REE of Choi state
nodes.statement: To calculate upper bound on the MDI-QKD capacity, it suffices to consider the relative entropy of entanglement of the Choi state of associated multiplex channel $\mathcal{N}^{\text{MDI},\mathcal{E}}_{\vv{A}\to \vv{Z}}$ as it is tele-covariant.
nodes.statement_short: By tele-covariance it suffices to compute the REE of the Choi state.

nodes.name: Erasure channel action
nodes.statement_short: Write the action of the erasure channel.

nodes.name: Choi state of the erasure links
nodes.statement_short: Compute the Choi state of the two erasure links.

nodes.name: Probabilistic Bell measurement
nodes.statement_short: Define the relay's Bell measurement with success probability $q$.

nodes.name: Output state
nodes.statement_short: Compute the output state after the measurement.

nodes.name: REE equals $q\eta_1\eta_2$
nodes.statement: This implies, the relative entropy of entanglement of the Choi state of $\mathcal{N}^{\text{MDI},\mathcal{E}}_{A_1A_2\to Z_1Z_2}$ is $q\eta_1\eta_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the REE of the Choi state is $q\eta_1\eta_2$.

nodes.name: MDI-QKD capacity with erasure links equals $q\eta_1\eta_2$
nodes.statement:
Employing Theorem~\ref{theo:E-alpha_bound}, the bipartite MDI-QKD capacity for the given MDI-QKD prototype with erasure channels is  
\begin{equation} \wt{P}_{\operatorname{LOCC}}(\mathcal{N}^{\text{MDI},\{\mathcal{E}_i\}_{i=1}^2})=q\eta_1\eta_2,
\end{equation}
as $q\eta_1\eta_2$ \textit{bits} is an achievable rate for the given setup  (see Refs.~\cite{GES16,PLOB15,WTB16} for the private capacities of $\mathcal{E}_{A_i\to C_i}$). Notice that $q\eta_1\eta_2$ is a strong converse bound.
assumptions: the given MDI-QKD prototype with erasure channels
conclusions: Notice that $q\eta_1\eta_2$ is a strong converse bound.
nodes.statement_short: The dual-rail MDI-QKD capacity with erasure links of transmissivities $\eta_i$ and Bell success $q$ is exactly $q\eta_1\eta_2$.

nodes.name: Comparison with the repeaterless (RB) bound
nodes.statement: For bipartite MDI-QKD (see Fig.~\ref{fig:mq-2-2}), using the results of Ref.~\cite{GES16,PLOB15} we get upper bound (RB) on the bipartite MDI-QKD capacity to be $\min\{\eta_1,\eta_2\}$ (e.g., see~\cite{CM17,pirandola2019capacities}). This bound is always looser than our strong converse upper bound $q\eta_1\eta_2$ bits for all practical purposes.

nodes.name: Distributing-party Devetak-Winter protocol for multiplex channels
nodes.statement_short: A distributing party measures and broadcasts classical side information; all others estimate her key variable (one-way DW protocol).

nodes.name: Fully separable input
nodes.statement: We begin with a fully separable pure state $\phi^n\in\operatorname{FS}\left(:\vv{A'^{ n}L}:\vv{B^{ n}R}:\vv{P}:\right)$. Here the notation $\vv{X^{ n}}$ means we consider $n$ copies of all subsystems $X_1,...,X_M$.
nodes.statement_short: Prepare $n$-copy fully separable pure input.

nodes.name: Apply channel isometries
nodes.statement: Application of $n$ copies of the isometric extension of multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'B}\to\vv{AC}}$ results in a pure state $\psi^n_{:\vv{A^{ n}L}:\vv{R}:\vv{C^{ n}P}:E^{n}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply $n$ copies of the channel's isometric extension.

nodes.name: Choose distributing party
nodes.statement: Let us now choose one party, ${\bf X}_i$, $i\in\{1,...,M\}$ as the distributing party.
nodes.statement_short: Choose distributing party

nodes.name: Distributing party measures
nodes.statement_short: Measure with POVM $\mc{Q}$ giving a cq state.

nodes.name: Classical post-processing and broadcast
nodes.statement: Party ${\bf X}_i$ then processes $X$ using classical channels $X\to Y$ and $Y\to Z$, where $Y=\{y,q(y)\}$ and  $Z=\{z,r(z)\}$ are classical random variables. $Y$ is kept by party ${\bf X}_i$ (to be used for the key) and $Z$ is broadcasted to all other trusted parties (and Eve).
nodes.statement_short: Process $X\to Y\to Z$, keep $Y$, broadcast $Z$.

nodes.name: Others estimate key
nodes.statement: Upon receiving $Z$, the other parties then perform their respective POVMs with the goal of estimating the key variable $Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Remaining parties measure to estimate $Y$.

nodes.name: Devetak-Winter one-way key rate
conclusions: obtains a common key with ${\bf X}$ at a rate $r_n^{i\to j}$ of
nodes.statement_short: Each party obtains a key with the distributing party at the Devetak-Winter rate $I(Y:X_j|Z)-I(Y:E^n|Z)$ per use.

nodes.name: Argument for the distributing-party lower bound
nodes.statement: Eq.~\eqref{eq59} has to be maximized over all free input states $\phi^n\in\operatorname{FS}\(:\vv{A'^{ n}L}:\vv{B^{ n}R}:\vv{P}:\)$, POVMs $\mc{Q}$ as well as classical channels $X\to Y$ and $Y\to Z$. As discussed in Ref.~\cite{AH09}, a conference key among all trusted parties can be obtained at the worst case rate between any pair $({\bf X}_i,{\bf X}_j)$. We also have the freedom to choose the distributing party.
nodes.statement_short: Optimize the DW rate over inputs and post-processing, take the worst pair, then maximize over the distributing party.

nodes.name: Optimize DW rate
nodes.statement: Eq.~\eqref{eq59} has to be maximized over all free input states $\phi^n\in\operatorname{FS}\(:\vv{A'^{ n}L}:\vv{B^{ n}R}:\vv{P}:\)$, POVMs $\mc{Q}$ as well as classical channels $X\to Y$ and $Y\to Z$.
nodes.statement_short: Maximize the DW rate over inputs, POVMs and classical channels.

nodes.name: Worst pair and best distributor
nodes.statement: As discussed in Ref.~\cite{AH09}, a conference key among all trusted parties can be obtained at the worst case rate between any pair $({\bf X}_i,{\bf X}_j)$. We also have the freedom to choose the distributing party.
nodes.statement_short: Conference key at worst pairwise rate, optimized over the distributing party.

nodes.name: Distributing-party lower bound on cppp conference key rate
conclusions: Putting it all together, we can achieve the following rate of conference key:
nodes.statement_short: cppp conference key rate is at least max over distributing party of the min pairwise DW rate.

nodes.name: Chain (permutation-ordered) Devetak-Winter protocol
nodes.statement_short: Parties ordered by a permutation each measure, keep a key variable and pass classical data to the next party (chain of one-way DW protocols).

nodes.name: Prepare input and apply channel
nodes.statement: As before, we begin with a fully separable pure state $\phi^n\in\operatorname{FS}\(:\vv{A'^{ n}L}:\vv{B^{ n}R}:\vv{P}:\)$ and apply $n$ copies of the isometric extension of multiplex channel $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'B}\to\vv{AC}}$, resulting in a pure state $\psi^n_{:\vv{A^{ n}L}:\vv{R}:\vv{C^{ n}P}:E^{n}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fully separable input through $n$ channel isometries.

nodes.name: Fix party ordering
nodes.statement: Assume now we are given some permutation $\sigma:\{1,...,M\}\to\{\sigma(1),...,\sigma(M)\}$, which determines the order in which the parties participate in the protocol.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a permutation fixing the order of parties.

nodes.name: First party measures
nodes.statement_short: First party measures, giving cq state $\omega^{(1)}$.

nodes.name: First party post-processes and sends
nodes.statement:
Party ${\bf X}_{\sigma(1)}$ then performs classical channels $X^{(1)}\to Y^{(1)}\to Z^{(1)}$, keeping random variable $Y^{(1)}$ and sending $Z^{(1)}$ to party ${\bf X}_{\sigma(2)}$. The corresponding c{\bf q} state is then given by 
\begin{equation} \tilde{\omega}^{(1)}_{c{\bf q}}=\sum_{x_1y_1z_1}r_1(z_1|y_1)q_1(y_1|x_1)p_1(x_1)\op{x_1y_1z_1}\otimes\omega^{x_1},
\end{equation}
where $\omega^{x_1}$ is the state of the remaining parties and Eve.
nodes.statement_short: Process $X^{(1)}\to Y^{(1)}\to Z^{(1)}$ and send $Z^{(1)}$ onward.

nodes.name: Next party measures adaptively
nodes.statement: Next, party ${\bf X}_{\sigma(2)}$ performs a POVM $\mc{Q}_{Z^{(1)}}^{(2)}$ on her share of $\omega^{x_{1}}$, which provides random variable ($X^{(2)}$. Party ${\bf X}_{\sigma(2)}$ then performs classical channels $Z^{(1)}X^{(2)}\to Y^{(2)}\to Z^{(2)}$, keeps $Y^{(2)}$ for herself and sends $Z^{(2)}$ to the next party ${\bf X}_{\sigma(3)}$, who applies the same procedure.
nodes.statement_short: Second party measures conditioned on $Z^{(1)}$, post-processes and forwards.

nodes.name: Iterate along the chain
nodes.statement: The protocol is repeated until party ${\bf X}_{\sigma(M)}$ receives $Z^{(M-1)}$, followed by her POVM and post-processing.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat until the last party.

nodes.name: cq state after $k$ steps
nodes.statement_short: Recursive form of the cq state after $k$ steps.

nodes.name: Argument for the chain lower bound
nodes.statement_short: Neighbouring parties get the DW rate; optimize, take the weakest link, and maximize over orderings.

nodes.name: Chain lower bound on cppp conference key rate
conclusions: Putting it all together, we can achieve the following rate of conference key:
nodes.statement_short: cppp conference key rate is at least the best ordering's weakest-link DW rate along the chain.

nodes.name: Bidirectional network (BN)
nodes.statement: In the BN, each of the nodes is connected with its neighbors by product bidirectional channels, which are specific bidirectional channels that is a tensor product of two point-to-point channels directed in opposite ways from each other.
nodes.section: 7.1 Lower bound for Bidirectional Network via spanning tree

nodes.name: The bidirectional network is a multiplex channel
nodes.statement: We first observe that BN is a particular case of a multiplex channel (call it $\cal N$). Indeed, in this case, all the parties are of type $\cal A$; i.e., they can read and write. The rule is that each party represented in the network as a vertex $v$ has $deg(v)$ of neighbors (see Ref.~\cite{Wil96book} for introduction to graph theory). Each party is assumed to write to her neighbors and also receive from these neighbors some quantum data.
nodes.section: 7.1 Lower bound for Bidirectional Network via spanning tree

nodes.name: Graph representation of a bidirectional network
nodes.statement: To be more specific, the BN can be represented by a weighted, directed multi-graph $G=(E,V)$ in which each edge $e_{ij}=(v_i,v_j) \in E$ represents a product bidirectional channel $\Lambda_{ij}=\Lambda_{i\rightarrow j} \otimes \Lambda_{j\rightarrow i}$ with weight $W:E\mapsto R_+$ such that $W(e_{ij})= W(e_{ji})={\cal P}(\Lambda_{i\rightarrow j})={\cal P}(\Lambda_{j\rightarrow i})$ (this edge can be represented by two directed edges: one from $v_i$ to $v_j$ and the other vice versa, hence the structure is directed multi-graph). Each product bidirectional channel has in both directions the same private capacity (that however may differ for different channels). By convention, we consider edges with index $i>j$ only.
nodes.section: 7.1 Lower bound for Bidirectional Network via spanning tree

nodes.name: Network size parameters $n=|V|$, $m=|E|$
nodes.statement: The number of nodes in the network is denoted as $|V|:=n$ and the number of edges as $|E|:=m$.
nodes.section: 7.1 Lower bound for Bidirectional Network via spanning tree

nodes.name: Star and path strategies are not tight on an example graph
nodes.statement:
As a motivation for the next consideration, there comes the fact that for such multiplex channels, the bounds given in inequalities~\eqref{eq:lb-star} and \eqref{eq:lb-path} above are not tight. We exemplify this on the graph presented in Fig.~\ref{fig:multigraph}(a). Namely, we assume that each red edge of the graph $G$ depicted there represents a (bidirectional) channel with private capacity $1$, while each blue - with this capacity equal to $2$. We do not depict all other edges (connections) as they have zero private capacity by assumption. We are ready to make two observations (i) approach of inequality~\eqref{eq:lb-star} would
    yield overall secret key agreement at rate $1$, as the only node connected all others in $G$ ($v_1$) contains
    (in fact, more than one) red edge. (ii) We observe by direct inspection that every path connecting all vertices also contains at least one red edge. On the other hand, there is a set of vertices [depicted with edges on Fig.~\ref{fig:multigraph}(b)] that forms the so-called {\it spanning tree} $T:=(V_T,E_T)\subset G$ of the graph $G$. Spanning tree is an acyclic connected subgraph of $G$, and the word "spanning" refers to the fact that all the vertices of the graph $G$ belong to $V_T$.
    It is easy to see that starting from any vertex of this tree, by the {\it breadth-first search } algorithm, one can visit all its edges, and one can obtain conference key at rate $2$ (see Ref.~\cite{LRCSbook} for introduction to algorithms).
nodes.section: 7.1 Lower bound for Bidirectional Network via spanning tree
nodes.statement_short: On the example graph the star and path bounds give rate 1 while a spanning tree avoiding red edges gives rate 2.

nodes.name: Spanning tree
nodes.statement: Spanning tree is an acyclic connected subgraph of $G$, and the word "spanning" refers to the fact that all the vertices of the graph $G$ belong to $V_T$.

conclusions: one easily comes up with the following lower bound, which is the main result of this section:
nodes.statement_short: BN conference key rate is at least the best spanning tree's weakest-edge DW rate, using breadth-first adaptive measurements.

nodes.name: Spanning-tree lower bound on the example graph
nodes.statement:
We exemplify the lower bound given in inequality~\eqref{eq:lb-general} with the Broadcast Network depicted on Fig.~\ref{fig:multigraph}. Let us first
focus on involved sets of vertices in the process of the breadth-first search over the tree $T$. The set of vertices of the spanning tree $T$ reads $\{v_1,...,v_6\}$. As the root vertex we choose $v_1$. Next $N_1[v_1] =\{v_2\}$, $N_2[v_1] =\{v_3,v_6\}$ and $N_3[v_1] =\{v_4,v_5\}$.
The presented lower bound reads in this case:
 \begin{align}
&\hat{P}_{\textnormal{cppp}}^{\mc{N}}\geq \nonumber
\\
&\max_{T\subseteq G}\min_{t\in V_T,t'\in N[t]} \lim_{n\to\infty}
\max_{\substack{\phi^n,\mc{Q}^{(1)},...,\mc{Q}^{(6)}\text{ POVM}\\X^{(v_1)}\to Y^{(v_1)}\to Z^{(v_1)},\\
        X^{(v_2)}Z^{(v_1)}\to Y^{(v_2)}\to Z^{(v_2)},\\
        X^{(v_3)}Z^{(v_2)}\to Y^{(v_3)}\to Z^{(v_3)},\\
            X^{(v_6)}Z^{(v_2)}\to Y^{(v_6)},\\
                X^{(v_5)}Z^{(v_3)}\to Y^{(v_5)},\\
                    X^{(v_4)}Z^{(v_3)}\to Y^{(v_4)}}}  r^{\sigma(t) \to \sigma(t')} \end{align}

nodes.name: Two-copy W-to-GHZ one-shot protocol
nodes.statement:
To accomplish this task, it
is sufficient to consider the initial state as being made up of two copies of the $\Phi_3^\mathrm{W}$ state. Then using results in Ref.~\cite{FL-2007}, it follows that we can obtain two $\Phi_2^+$ states in two distinct bipartite systems with a probability that is arbitrarily close to $\frac 23$; having this in mind, one can obtain $\Phi_3^\mathrm{GHZ}$ by employing ancilla and the entanglement swapping protocol~\cite{PhysRevLett.71.4287}. In this way, we calculated a lower bound on the distillation of $\Phi_3^\mathrm{GHZ}$ states from tow copies of $\Phi_3^\mathrm{W}$ state in one-shot regime (one $\Phi_3^\mathrm{GHZ}$ state with probability $\frac 23$ from two $\Phi_3^\mathrm{W}$ states).

This result is due to different definitions of biseparability; the state in Ref.~\cite{VDM-2002} is a tensor product with respect to one of the cuts, whereas we make use of convexity of the set of biseparable states. Indeed our states are biseparable by construction (see Sec. \ref{sec:ME}).

Analogously $[M+1]_{k}= [1,...,k-1,k_1,k_2,k+1,...,M+1]$ indicates the state in which subsystem $k$ was split into systems $k_1$ and $k_2$.

nodes.statement:
Hence in particular case of $\Phi_{3}^\mathrm{W}$ state we can also skip minimization with respect to $i$, $j$ since the state is symmetric. Using properties of entanglement measures \cite{Horodecki_2000,Ishizaka_2005,plenio2005introduction}, we have
\begin{align}
&K_D\left( \Phi_{3}^\mathrm{W}\right) \le 
K_D\left( \Phi_{2+1}^\mathrm{W}\right) \le E_r^{\infty}\left(\Phi_{2+1}^\mathrm{W}\right)\\
&=h_2\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\approx 0.9183~ \mathrm{bit},

nodes.name: Merging rule for multiplex channels
nodes.statement: It is natural that the analogies of Proposition~\ref{prop:statesmerging} and Corollary~\ref{cor:dist-state} hold for the multiplex quantum channel $\mc{N}$. The upper bound on $M$-partite multiplex quantum channel takes the form of $M-1$-partite multiplex channel, where the new party's type is determined according to the following rule: If the two parties are of the same type (say $B$), then the new type is the same as the same ($B$ in that case). If the types are different, then the new type becomes always $A$ because, e.g., when $B$ and $C$ are merged, they have the ability to both read and write.

nodes.name: Network channels as special cases of multiplex channels
nodes.statement:
All network channels possible in a communication setting are special cases of multiplex quantum channels $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to\vv{A}\vv{C}}$ (see Fig.~\ref{fig:mpc}), e.g.,
\begin{enumerate}
\item Point-to-point quantum channel: This is a quantum channel of the form $\mathcal{N}_{B_b\to C_c}$ with a single sender and
a single receiver. When a multiplex quantum channel has the form $\mathcal{N}_{B_b\to
C_c}$ then $\mathscr{A}=\emptyset$ and $|\mathscr{B}|=1=|\mathscr{C}|$. This is arguably
the simplest form of a communication (network) channel as it involves only two parties with
one party sending input to the channel and the other receiving the output from the channel.
\item Bidirectional quantum channel: This is a multiplex quantum channel of the form $\mc{N}_{A_1'A_2'\to A_1A_2}$ with two parties who are
both senders and receivers, i.e. $|\mathscr{A}|=2$ and $\mathscr{B}=\emptyset=\mathscr{C}$ (cf.~\cite{D18thesis,BHLS03}).




\item Quantum interference channel: This is a bipartite quantum channel of the form $\mc{N}_{B_1B_2\to C_1C_2}$ with two senders and two receivers (cf.~\cite{FHSSW11}). We may also call $\mc{N}_{\vv{B}\to \vv{C}}$ with an equal number of senders and receivers as quantum interference channel. \item Broadcast quantum channel: This is a multipartite quantum channel of the form $\mc{N}_{B_b\to \vv{C}}$ with a single sender and multiple receivers (cf.~\cite{D05,YHD2006}). We may also call $\mc{N}_{\vv{B}\to\vv{C}}$ as a broadcast channel if the number of senders is less than the number of receivers. 
\item Multiple access quantum channel: This is a multipartite quantum channel of the form $\mc{N}_{\vv{B}\to C_c}$ with multiple senders and a single receiver (cf.~\cite{YHD05MQAC}). We may also call $\mc{N}_{\vv{B}\to\vv{C}}$ as a multiple access channel if the number of senders is more than the number of receivers. 
\item Physical box: Any physical box with quantum or classical inputs and quantum or classical outputs.
\item Network quantum channels of types $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\to \vv{A}\vv{C}}$ and $\mc{N}_{\vv{A'}\vv{B}\to \vv{A}}$. 
\end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Point-to-point, bidirectional, interference, broadcast and multiple-access channels and physical boxes are multiplex channels.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: We begin by showing the bound for pure biseparable states $\ket{\varphi}_{\vv{KS}}$. For such a state there exists a bipartition of the parties, defined by nonempty index sets $I\subset\{1,...,M\}$ and $J=\{1,...,M\}\setminus I$, such that the state is product with respect to that bipartition. Namely $\ket{\varphi}_{\vv{KS}}=\ket{\widetilde\varphi}_{S_{I}K_{I}}\otimes\ket{\overline\varphi}_{S_{J}K_{J}}$, where we have defined $\mc{H}_{S_{I}K_{I}}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}\mc{H}_{S_{i}K_{i}}$ and $\mc{H}_{S_{J}K_{J}}=\bigotimes_{j\in J}\mc{H}_{S_{j}K_{j}}$. Let us also define $m:=|I|$ and $n:=|J|$ and note that $M=m+n$. We can expand \begin{align} &\ket{\widetilde\varphi}_{S_{I}K_{I}}=\sum_{i_1,...,i_{m}=0}^{K-1}\widetilde{\alpha}_{i_1...i_{m}}\ket{i_1...i_{m}}_{K_{I}}\otimes\ket{\widetilde{\phi}_{i_1...i_{m}}}_{S_{I}}\\ &\ket{\overline\varphi}_{S_{J}K_{J}}=\sum_{j_1,...,j_{n}=0}^{K-1}\overline{\alpha}_{j_1...j_{n}}\ket{j_1...j_{n}}_{K_J}\otimes\ket{\overline{\phi}_{j_1...j_{n}}}_{S_J}. \end{align} Here $\widetilde{\alpha}_{i_1...i_{m}}\in\bbm{C}$ such that $\sum_{i_1,...,i_{m}=0}^{K-1}|\widetilde{\alpha}_{i_1...i_{m}}|^2=1$ and $\overline{\alpha}_{j_1...j_{n}}\in\bbm{C}$ such that $\sum_{j_1,...,j_{n}=0}^{K-1}|\overline{\alpha}_{j_1...j_{n}}|^2=1$. Further it holds \begin{widetext} \begin{align} \operatorname{Tr}\left[\Pi^{\gamma,K}_{\vv{KS}}\varphi_{\vv{KS}}\right] &=\operatorname{Tr}\left[\(\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i,k=0}^{K-1}\(\ket{i}\bra{k}\)^{\otimes M}_{\vv{K}}\otimes U_{\vv{S}}^{(i^M)}U_{\vv{S}}^{(k^M)\dag}\)\widetilde\varphi_{K_IS_I}\otimes\overline\varphi_{K_JS_J}\right]\\ &=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i,k=0}^{K-1}\widetilde{\alpha}_{i^{m}}\overline{\alpha}_{i^{n}}(\widetilde{\alpha}_{k^{m}})^*(\overline{\alpha}_{k^{n}})^*\operatorname{Tr}\left[U^{(i^M)\dag}\ket{\widetilde{\phi}_{i^m}}\bra{\widetilde{\phi}_{k^m}}_{S_I}\otimes\ket{\overline{\phi}_{i^n}}\bra{\overline{\phi}_{k^n}}_{S_J}U^{(k^M)}\right]\\ &=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i,k=0}^{K-1}\widetilde{\alpha}_{i^m}\overline{\alpha}_{i^n}(\widetilde{\alpha}_{k^m})^*(\overline{\alpha}_{k^n})^*\bra{\zeta_k}\ket{\zeta_i}, \end{align} \end{widetext} where we have defined the state \begin{equation} \ket{\zeta_i}_{\vv{S}} \coloneqq U^{(i^M)\dag}\ket{\widetilde{\phi}_{i^m}}_{S_I}\otimes\ket{\overline{\phi}_{i^n}}_{S_J}. \end{equation} We note that eq. (\ref{eq:9}) is a probability, in particular it is real and non-negative. Hence it holds \begin{align} &\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i,k=0}^{K-1}\widetilde{\alpha}_{i^m}\overline{\alpha}_{i^n}(\widetilde{\alpha}_{k^m})^*(\overline{\alpha}_{k^n})^*\bra{\zeta_k}\ket{\zeta_i}\\ &=\left|\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i,k=0}^{K-1}\widetilde{\alpha}_{i^m}\overline{\alpha}_{i^n}(\widetilde{\alpha}_{k^m})^*(\overline{\alpha}_{k^n})^*\bra{\zeta_k}\ket{\zeta_i}\right|\\ &\leq\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i,k=0}^{K-1}\left|\widetilde{\alpha}_{i^m}\right|\left|\overline{\alpha}_{i^n}\right|\left|\widetilde{\alpha}_{k^m}\right|\left|\overline{\alpha}_{k^n}\right|\left|\bra{\zeta_k}\ket{\zeta_i}\right| \end{align} where in the first inequality we have used the subadditivity and multiplicity of the absolute value of complex numbers. We note that for all $i,k$ in the sum $\left|\bra{\zeta_k}\ket{\zeta_i}\right|\leq 1$. Let us define $p_i=\left|\widetilde{\alpha}_{i^m}\right|^2$ and note that $p_i\geq0$ and $\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}p_i\leq1$. Let us also define $q_i=\left|\overline{\alpha}_{i^n}\right|^2$ and note that $q_i\geq0$ and $\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}q_i\leq1$. Hence there exist respective probability distributions $\{\hat{p}_i\}$ and $\{\hat{q}_i\}$ over $\{0,...,K-1\}$ such that $p_i\leq\hat{p}_i$ and $q_i\leq\hat{q}_i$ for all $i=0,...,K-1$. We then obtain \begin{align} &\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i,k=0}^{K-1}\left|\widetilde{\alpha}_{i^m}\right|\left|\overline{\alpha}_{i^n}\right|\left|\widetilde{\alpha}_{k^m}\right|\left|\overline{\alpha}_{k^n}\right|\left|\bra{\zeta_k}\ket{\zeta_i}\right|\\ &\leq\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i,k=0}^{K-1}\sqrt{p_iq_ip_kq_k} =\frac{1}{K}\left[\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}\sqrt{p_iq_i}\right]^2\\ &\leq\frac{1}{K}\left[\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}\sqrt{\hat{p}_i\hat{q}_i}\right]^2\leq\frac{1}{K}, \end{align} where we have used that the classical fidelity between two probability distributions is upper bounded by $1$. This establishes the theorem for pure biseparable states with respect to arbitrary bipartitions. Noting that every mixed biseparable state $\sigma_{\vv{KS}}\in\operatorname{BS}(:\vv{KS}:)$ can be expressed as a convex sum of pure biseparable states finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Expand a pure biseparable state in the key basis and bound the test probability by a classical fidelity, giving $1/K$; extend by convexity.

nodes.statement: We begin by showing the bound for pure biseparable states $\ket{\varphi}_{\vv{KS}}$. For such a state there exists a bipartition of the parties, defined by nonempty index sets $I\subset\{1,...,M\}$ and $J=\{1,...,M\}\setminus I$, such that the state is product with respect to that bipartition.  Namely $\ket{\varphi}_{\vv{KS}}=\ket{\widetilde\varphi}_{S_{I}K_{I}}\otimes\ket{\overline\varphi}_{S_{J}K_{J}}$, where we have defined $\mc{H}_{S_{I}K_{I}}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}\mc{H}_{S_{i}K_{i}}$ and $\mc{H}_{S_{J}K_{J}}=\bigotimes_{j\in J}\mc{H}_{S_{j}K_{j}}$.
